Context: Zimmermann is building a Salesforce PWA Kit storefront (www.zimmermann.com). Confluence space key is likely "SFCC". I am pre-build planning three Jira stories and need to know what documentation exists that bears on them, and whether any of it contradicts the tickets.

The three stories:
- SFCC-236 "Product Card Shared Component" — ONE shared product card component with display variations (Homepage, PLP, Wishlist, Recently Viewed Full History) driven by a style prop. Labels: PRC-09, SPR-01, SPR-02, SPR-10..SPR-16, Squad-A. Epic SFCC-2 "PWA Kit Components".
- SFCC-83 "Recently Viewed UI Component (Shared)" — horizontal rail of recently-viewed product tiles, surfaces PLP/PDP/Cart. Guest = session-only storage; authenticated = cross-session, cross-device, stored against the customer account. Labels: PRD-027, SPR-61, DesignDependent. Epic SFCC-7 "Search & Recommendations".
- SFCC-84 "Recently Viewed - See Full History" — the page behind the "See Full History" link. Labels: PRD-027, SPR-61, DesignDependent. Epic SFCC-7.

Search Confluence for and REPORT ON:
1. Any TSD (Technical Solution Design) covering product card / product tile / shared components / recently viewed / browsing history. Note the official TSD parent page is 392888324 — check its children.
2. Any PRD or functional-requirements page matching requirement IDs: PRC-09, PRD-027, SPR-01, SPR-02, SPR-10, SPR-11, SPR-12, SPR-13, SPR-14, SPR-16, SPR-61. These look like requirement IDs from a functional requirements spreadsheet — find the page that defines them and quote what each of the ones you can find actually says.
3. Anything on "Recently Viewed" — especially: where browsing history is STORED for authenticated shoppers (SFCC customer profile custom attribute? Einstein? Omneo? Data Cloud? localStorage?), retention period, and consent treatment.
4. Anything on component reuse / component library / design system / atomic structure (atoms-molecules-organisms) that governs how a shared component should be built.
5. Anything on PLP or Homepage or Wishlist UI that specifies product tile contents.
6. Any page about consent gating that would apply to browsing history (Didomi).

For EVERY page you find, report: page title, page ID, last-updated date, and a tight summary of what it says that is relevant. CRITICALLY: flag any place where the Confluence documentation CONTRADICTS the ticket summaries above, or describes an approach that sounds different from what the tickets describe.

If you find NOTHING for a given topic, say so explicitly and clearly — "no TSD exists for X" is a first-class finding I need, not a failure. Do not pad with irrelevant pages.

## 3. Recently Viewed — storage, retention, consent

### Where it is stored: not designed anywhere

The **only** storage statement in the entire space is the SPR-61 clause: *"stored in the browser session and persisted cross-session on login."* That is it.

- **No SFCC customer profile custom attribute** is named anywhere.
- **No Einstein, Omneo, or Data Cloud** involvement is documented for browsing history. (Einstein appears only for recommendations and search — SPR-42, SPR-58, SPR-63.)
- `localStorage` / `sessionStorage` / "session storage" appear **nowhere** in any requirement page or in the PWA TSD.
- No cap, no dedupe rule, no cross-region behaviour, and **no anonymous→authenticated merge rule** — despite that merge being the single hardest part of the feature.

### Retention: no period is documented anywhere

Exhaustively checked. The only retention requirement is **REG-062**: *"The system will allow data retention periods to be configured in SFCC Business Manager per market. Customer PII will be automatically purged upon expiry of the configured retention period."* — it defers the value entirely and nobody has supplied one.

For contrast, wishlist *does* have a number: **CRM-140** comment — *"Suggested threshold 18 months - OOTB SFCC for guest users is 7 days for logged in users we need to define custom logic to clear wishlist."* Recently Viewed has no equivalent.

**Unflagged consequence:** if history is written against the customer account, it becomes PII and inherits **REG-060** (right-to-erasure), **REG-065** (DSAR export) and **REG-062** (per-market purge). No document acknowledges this, and TSD §11.3 pushes GDPR fulfilment out of PWA scope entirely.

### Consent: a formally open question owned by Legal
